        - paragraph: In simple English
        - heading "Understand Connected Components" [level=2]
        - paragraph: A connected component is a largest group of vertices where each pair is connected by some path. You can learn Connected Components by trying one small example instead of long theory.
        - paragraph: A connected component is a largest group of vertices where each pair is connected by some path. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
        - paragraph: "In real life, islands and bridges: Separate island groups form components. Watch out: Thinking vertices need a direct edge to be in the same component. A path through other vertices is enough."

      - article:
        - heading "2. NOTICE THE PATTERN" [level=3]
        - paragraph: • Vertices A, B, C reach each other.
        - paragraph: • Vertices D, E, F reach each other.
        - paragraph: • Vertex G is alone.
        - paragraph: • No vertex in one group can reach a vertex in another group.
        - paragraph: Each group is a connected component.
      - article:
        - heading "3. UNDERSTAND THE RULE" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Two vertices u and v are in the same connected component if there exists a path between them.
        - paragraph: "Definition: A connected component is a maximal set of vertices such that every pair is connected by a path."
        - paragraph: "Key fact: Components partition the vertex set."
        - status:
          - text: V(G) = C₁ ⊔ C₂ ⊔ ··· ⊔ Cₖ
          - generic: (disjoint union)
      - article:
        - heading "4. WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Find the connected components.
        - paragraph: "Solution:"
        - paragraph: "Components are {A,B,C}, {D,E,F}, {G}."
        - paragraph: Total components = 3.
      - article:
        - heading "⚠ COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Having an edge between components makes them one component.
        - paragraph: "Reality: A component has no edges connecting it to any other component."
      - article:
        - text: "Example: If we add an edge between C and D, components change."
